txt: It has only lasted three seconds. The girl still waits for her answer.
Lamby is a stuffed lamb that, admittedly, has seen better days. One of the eye-buttons is missing and the fur is tattered in several parts.
Lamby remains silent. The fireplace flickers and cackles. She hugs the doll close to her chest and laughs.
She clutches a small stuffed animal. Occasionally she twirls it around.
She frowns, delaying divulging her secret. "Oo-kay," she says finally with some reluctance. "I hid them inside my sandcastle. Behind the house." She points somewhere outside. "You can take them."
She gasps. "No! Don't say bad words! Promise?"
She pouts. "I hid them. The twins were going to take them. They're stupid..." She lifts her stuffed toy up and looks into its one remaining eye, as though searching for confirmation.
She stares at you, waiting for an answer.
She turns the stuffed lamb to face her. "What does that mean, Lamby?" The doll offers no reply. Stuffing hangs out its rear.
She twirls the furry doll around in the air, giggling happily.
The little girl tilts her head. "Do you promise you won't say bad words anymore?"
"*Everything*!" She shouts with glee.
"Bye!" The girl's large, curious eyes remain fixed on you.
"Cap-capi-capeel..." She struggles to pronounce the words. She shakes her head. "No."
"Found them when Lamby and I were playing hide-and-seek. In an empty house where no one lives! I think someone hid them there..."
"Good." She hugs Lamby close to her again.
"Haa ha haa!" She continues laughing. "Lamby tells them part." She waves her fuzzy doll in the air.
"Haa haa, yessss!" She smiles, hugging her fuzzy toy.
"Hello, mister!" A young girl, barely four or five years old, sits on the sofa. She is looking at you with frank curiosity.
"Hello, mister!" The Net Picker's daughter waves at you.
"I dunno."
"Isn't he soft?" She's right, Lamby is very soft. She rubs the white fur against your cheek, then returns the lamb into her lap, cuddling it.
"It's Lamby! He's my friend. Sort of, like..." She holds the fuzzy beast up to demonstrate.
"It's a *grouse*," she yelps, smiling broadly.
"It's old and broken." She nods. "Dan-ze-ruus, Mom says. I listen to mom. Lamby also listens. Brothers listen. They tried going there, but it was scary and they ran away!"
"Lamby doesn't like bad words. Please promise!"
"Lamby usually doesn't like strangers, but you're also fuzzy like Lamby."
"Ll... Luby... Rr... R-luuby." Suddenly the girl gets all serious and leans in, as if she's about to tell you a secret.
"Mhmh," she replies, nodding. "It's very, very booky."
"My mom tells me that I'm a big girl, but she doesn't know that I can't say *ll*. Or like, sometimes I can, but then... *ll*... *rr*... *llrr*..."
"My mom's outside, and I don't really know about my dad." She gives you a bright smile like it's a good thing.
"Noo, mister!" Her eyes grow wider as she shakes her head. "Even Lamby doesn't like it." She hugs her stuffed toy tighter.
"Noo-noooo, that's not it." She frowns, looking at her tattered toy. "You know what you are, Lamby."
"Nooooo! Don't be bad too!" Her face bunches up in a scowl.
"Ohh, okay!" She nods seriously.
"Ohh, okay!" She twirls her fuzzy beast in the air.
"Okay, then. I'm sorry." She presses her own cheek against Lamby and smiles, sadly.
"Oooh..." She doesn't seem to understand, but the lieutenant's tone has conveyed to her the 'important' part.
"Oooh..." She doesn't seem to understand, but you have conveyed the 'important' part, at least.
"Ooooh." She looks alarmed. "I had gloves, very big ones! Heavy too."
"Sure! I mean you already took it. I don't like it anyway... it looks angry."
"Sure! Just go and get it. I don't like it anyway... it looks angry."
"That's nice! My mom is great," she nods. "She's never angry or anything."
"They look the same! Haa ha haa! Sometimes I can't tell them 'part."
"They look... ai-dent-ik!" She slowly processes the word, then snickers with laughter.
"They're in my sandcastle." She points somewhere outside. "Behind our house. Under the sand. You can break the castle, it's not very good."
"Uh huh," she nods. "Mom is great! You know what's great about my mom?"
"Uh, mister, what were you doing in my fireplace?"
"Uhhhhh..." She sits her doll on her lap. Its ragged limbs reach out toward you, as if longing for a cuddle. "Like what?"
"Vee-eery booky!" She's clutching her stuffed toy and shaking her head. "Don't go there."
"We don't go there. Mom and auntie think we do, but it's very booky."
"What?" She covers Lamby's ears by cupping his whole head in her small palms.
"Why?" She looks at you suspiciously.
"Yep!" The girl nods firmly. "I don't say bad words. Lamby doesn't either."
"Yes!" She lights with recognition. "The twins got in trouble for saying *bad words*."
"Yes. Very soft." Suddenly she pushes the stuffed animal toward your face.
"Yes." She yawns, and leans back into the cushion.
"Yesss." She frowns. "They don't want to play with me. They're older and play outside!"
"Yessss, Lamby has lived a long life." She waves the lamb around in the air. "Lamby was a... re.. a rev..." She stumbles on her words.
"Yessss," she yelps happily! "Lamby was a re-luz-ion...ry."
"Yesssss, I am! Little Lily!" She gazes at you with her big eyes. "You know my mom?"
"You're welcome!"
